lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write Jordan’s materials list and a numbered making sequence for the cardboard organiser. Include when scissors are used, where the adult must be, and how pieces join without a knife or power tool.

FEEDBACK
Materials are cardboard, marking paper, a pencil and scissors; an adult is nearby for every cut. Order: measure and mark a base within 15 cm, cut with scissors, fold, slot tabs into slits, then press edges flat. Joining is by slots, not by a knife or a hot tool. Power tools are not in a Year 7 paper plan. Cutting before measuring is not a step in this sequence.

WATCH FOR
Planning a craft knife or a hot glue gun because it seems faster than scissors and slots. Those tools are outside this paper brief and need a different safety setup. Keep scissors as the only cutter, keep an adult nearby, and join cardboard by slotting.

WORKED MODEL
Jordan’s plan uses cardboard and scissors only, with an adult nearby, and joins pieces by slotted tabs. Materials: one cereal-box panel, scrap paper, a pencil for marking, and scissors. Sequence: measure a base no wider than 15 cm and mark it; cut on the line with scissors while an adult is in the room; fold the walls; cut short tabs and slits and slot them together; press every edge flat so nothing scratches.
